question.text: What will be the seasonally adjusted month-on-month percentage change in New Zealand's total electronic card transaction values for October 2026 (Stats NZ, released 12 November 2026)?
question.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves to the seasonally adjusted month-on-month percentage change in the total value of electronic card transactions (all industries, i.e. including the services and other non-retail categories) for October 2026, as reported in Stats NZ's information release "Electronic card transactions: October 2026", published on 12 November 2026 at 10:45am NZDT and listed at https://www.stats.govt.nz/information-releases/.

The resolving figure is the percentage Stats NZ states in that release for the change in the seasonally adjusted total value of electronic card spending — the figure in the sentence of the form "the total value of electronic card spending, including the two non-retail categories (services and other non-retail), [increased/decreased] from September 2026, up/down $X million (Y percent)". For example, the September 2026 release reported "down $51 million (0.5 percent)", which corresponds to -0.5.

If the October 2026 release does not state a percentage for the total (all industries) series, the question instead resolves to the percentage change between the seasonally adjusted total values for September 2026 and October 2026 published in that release.
question.fine_print: Resolution uses the figures as first published in the release of 12 November 2026; later revisions to seasonally adjusted levels do not change the answer. If that release is delayed, resolution waits until it is published.

research:
## October 2026 NZ electronic card spending (seasonally adjusted total, month on month): research notes

### 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-02: I fetched the Stats NZ September 2026 release page, but only the page title came back, so I could not check the text directly. Its stated next release, "Electronic card transactions: October 2026", is on 12 November 2026 at 10:45am NZDT. [Stats NZ](https://www.stats.govt.nz/information-releases/electronic-card-transactions-september-2026/)
- 2026-10-16: Xinhua's report of the September release confirms the total fell 0.5% (down NZ$51m) to NZ$9.2b, with 167m transactions averaging NZ$55. Retail fell 0.4% (NZ$30m) and core retail fell 0.7% (NZ$41m). Non-retail excluding services fell NZ$25m (1.1%) and services fell NZ$5.9m (1.5%). The total rose 0.3% for the September quarter compared with the June quarter. [The Star/Xinhua](https://www.thestar.com.my/news/world/2026/10/16/new-zealand-electronic-card-spending-down-05-pct-in-september)
- Trading Economics reports September as -0.4% month on month and August as -0.9%, with July revised up to +1.2%. The -0.4% matches Stats NZ's retail figure, not the total. TE's August and July numbers may also be retail, so they don't line up cleanly with the series this question uses. [TE Sep](https://tradingeconomics.com/new-zealand/credit-card-spending/news/592524), [TE Aug](https://tradingeconomics.com/new-zealand/credit-card-spending/news/575559)

### 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. No official or private October 2026 card-spending figure has been published. I could not find October Paymark/Cuscal data. It usually comes out in the first week of the following month, so it may appear before 12 November.

### 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-02: Centrix says annual business liquidations rose 18%. The hospitality liquidation rate is 3.3 times the all-sector average, and Centrix says pressure is "concentrated in some consumer-facing industries". [NZ Herald](https://www.nzherald.co.nz/business/annual-liquidations-up-18-as-retail-hospitality-closures-surge/NMZAEAMMTZD7NIKPWA7UP4324U/)
- 2026-11-02: Parental income testing for Jobseeker payments starts, affecting about 4,300 people aged 18 to 19. This is a small effect. [RNZ](https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/politics/2302738/thousands-of-young-people-lose-access-to-unemployment-benefits)
- 2026-10-26: Global Petrol Prices lists 95-octane at about NZ$3.73, up 12.7% on a month earlier. Fuel To Go's discounted card price for 91 eased from $3.610 to $3.512 in late October. MBIE's weekly data runs to 23 October, but I could not extract the figures. [GPP](https://www.globalpetrolprices.com/New-Zealand/gasoline_prices/), [Fuel To Go](https://fueltogo.co.nz/national-pricing-fuel-card), [MBIE](https://www.mbie.govt.nz/building-and-energy/energy-and-natural-resources/energy-statistics-and-modelling/energy-statistics/weekly-fuel-price-monitoring)
- 2026-10-16: Petrol rose 6.4% in September and 24.3% over the year, per Stats NZ selected price indexes. [mpamag](https://www.mpamag.com/nz/news/general/nz-petrol-prices-jump-64-as-banks-split-on-inflation-outlook/593800)
- 2026-10-16: Retail NZ says retail is "entering the key last quarter under real pressure". Fuel is behind most of the nominal gains, while apparel (-5.2%) and hospitality (-4.4%) are weak. [Scoop](https://business.scoop.co.nz/2026/10/16/retail-entering-key-last-quarter-under-real-pressure/)
- Around 2026-10-05: The 91 petrol average hit a record above $3.50 a litre. [1News](https://www.1news.co.nz/2026/10/05/petrol-price-hits-all-time-high-as-average-litre-of-91-tops-350/)
- Early October 2026: Paymark core retail for September was $3.57b, down 1.3% year on year, which it blamed on petrol, interest rates and weather. Fuel spending was running about 35% above a year earlier in the week to 30 September. Paymark called it a "slower start" to the pre-Christmas period. [NZ Herald](https://www.nzherald.co.nz/business/retail-figures-spending-falls-in-september-as-consumers-cope-with-rising-petrol-prices-interest-rates-bad-weather/BC24F3PVWVCBPMXNNAAUQCFW3E/), [Newswire](https://newswire.co.nz/2026/10/new-zealand-retail-spending-september-2026-paymark/)
- 2026-10-02: ANZ-Roy Morgan consumer confidence was 97.6 for September, below 100. The October reading was due 30 October, but I could not find it. [ANZ](https://www.anz.co.nz/content/dam/anzconz/documents/economics-and-market-research/2026/ANZ-ConsumerConfidence-20261002.pdf)
- 2026-11-08: A general election is due, with National at 0.70 to win on Polymarket. Campaigning may have a small effect on October sentiment.

### 4. Base rates
- Total series in 2026 (from the question background): January -0.7, April -1.6, May +2.2, July +1.0 (TE says revised to about +1.2), August about -0.9 (unverified as the total figure), September -0.5. The Q3 total was +0.3% on Q2.
- 2026-10 vs 2025-10: TE reports October 2025 total ECT at +0.2% month on month. [TE](https://tradingeconomics.com/new-zealand/credit-card-spending/news/501505)
- Typical size of moves: monthly changes in the total are mostly within ±1%, with occasional ±1.5 to 2.2% swings. The sign changes often, and large moves tend to partly reverse the next month.
- What this means for October: if pump prices kept rising into early October, fuel spending (nominal) gives a mechanical lift. Two straight declines (August and September) leave room for some bounce back. Hospitality and discretionary spending remain weak.

### 5. Other forecasts
- No Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or Metaculus market matches this question. The Kalshi markets supplied (Amazon, McDonald's, Afterpay and others) are US credit card spend indices and don't apply. The NZ election markets on Polymarket are only background context.
- I found no published economist consensus for October ECT. Bank previews (ASB, Westpac, ANZ) usually come out the week of the release.

### 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- First week of November: Paymark/Cuscal October retail spending data, the most useful early indicator if it appears.
- About 2026-10-30, already out: the ANZ-Roy Morgan October consumer confidence reading.
- 2026-11-08: NZ general election.
- 2026-11-12, 10:45am NZDT: the Stats NZ October ECT release, which decides the question. Seasonal adjustment may revise September; only the October percentage as first published counts.
- After resolution: Stats NZ selected price indexes (17 November) and RBNZ C13 card data (20 or 21 November; sources give both dates).

I'm writing up the findings now. I couldn't read the Stats NZ September release page itself, so some figures below come from secondary sources and are marked as such.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-10-16: Stats NZ published "Electronic card transactions: September 2026". When I fetched the page, only the title came back, so I could not check the headline total of -0.5% (-$51m) against the primary source. [Stats NZ](https://www.stats.govt.nz/information-releases/electronic-card-transactions-september-2026/)
- 2026-10-16: Trading Economics gives the seasonally adjusted figure for September as -0.4% m/m after -0.9% in August, and +0.9% y/y (August was +0.2%). By industry: fuel +2.9%, hospitality -2.3%, apparel -2.0%, durables -0.4%, consumables +0.3%, motor vehicles +0.6%. It says July was revised from +1.3% to +1.2%. Its -0.4% probably refers to the retail series, since the question puts retail at -0.4% and the all-industries total at -0.5%. [Trading Economics](https://tradingeconomics.com/new-zealand/credit-card-spending/news/592524)
- 2026-10-16: InvestingLive gives retail at -0.4% for September and -0.9% for August. It does not report an all-industries total. [InvestingLive](https://investinglive.com/news/new-zealand-card-spending-falls-for-second-month-as-food-prices-hold-flat-in-september/)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. The October release is due on 12 November. I found no October card data from Stats NZ, Paymark, ANZ or the other banks.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-02: Centrix reports annual business liquidations up 18%. Hospitality liquidations run at 3.3 times the all-sector rate, which points to continued stress in consumer-facing industries. [NZ Herald](https://www.nzherald.co.nz/business/annual-liquidations-up-18-as-retail-hospitality-closures-surge/NMZAEAMMTZD7NIKPWA7UP4324U/)
- 2026-11-02: Parental income testing for Jobseeker payments for 18 and 19 year olds takes effect. This is after October, so it does not affect the October figure. [RNZ](https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/politics/2302738/thousands-of-young-people-lose-access-to-unemployment-benefits)
- 2026-10-28: The RBNZ held the OCR at 2.75%, after a 25bp hike on 2 September. [RBNZ](https://www.rbnz.govt.nz/en), [Forex Fundamentals](https://forexfundamentals.com/economic-calendar/rbnz/2026-10-28)
- 2026-10-26: GlobalPetrolPrices puts NZ gasoline at NZ$3.73/L, up 12.7% on a month earlier. One weekly BP 91 price fell to $3.512 from $3.610 the week before, which may hint at easing late in the month, but that is a single unconfirmed data point. [GlobalPetrolPrices](https://www.globalpetrolprices.com/New-Zealand/gasoline_prices/), [Fuel To Go](https://fueltogo.co.nz/national-pricing-fuel-card)
- 2026-10-16: The Gaspy average for 91 was $3.61/L and diesel $3.23/L. Some stations charged over $4 for 95. [1News](https://www.1news.co.nz/2026/10/16/fuel-price-tops-4-at-the-pump/)
- 2026-10-16: ASB's Kim Mundy said the main headwinds on consumers should ease next year. Retail NZ said households are cautious, with apparel and hospitality weak. [NZCity](https://home.nzcity.co.nz/news/article.aspx?id=456103&fm=psp%2Ctst), [Scoop](https://business.scoop.co.nz/2026/10/16/retail-entering-key-last-quarter-under-real-pressure/)
- 2026-10-06: Paymark reported September core retail at $3.572bn, -1.3% y/y, after -1.8% in August. Fuel spending was about 35% above a year earlier in the last week of September, mostly because of prices. [Scoop](https://business.scoop.co.nz/2026/10/06/retail-spending-stalls-before-crucial-last-quarter/), [RNZ](https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/business/1744906/petrol-rates-and-weather-consumer-spending-hit-by-three-tough-knocks)
- 2026-10-05: 91 petrol hit a record national average above $3.50/L. Brent has stayed above US$100 for a sustained period. [1News](https://www.1news.co.nz/2026/10/05/petrol-price-hits-all-time-high-as-average-litre-of-91-tops-350/)

Taken together: card spending is in nominal terms, so higher fuel prices in October would push the fuel category up, while discretionary categories have been weak.

## 4. Base rates
- Seasonally adjusted total changes for 2026, from the question: Jan -0.7, Apr -1.6, May +2.2, Jul +1.0, Sep -0.5. Secondary sources give August at -0.9% and July revised to +1.2%, but those figures may be for the retail series rather than the total.
- Monthly moves usually fall between about -1.6% and +2.2%. Many are within ±1%. Over 2026 there has been no consistent direction.
- Recent momentum is negative, with two straight monthly falls (August and September). Annual growth is weak, at roughly 0 to 1% y/y.
- The RBNZ credit card series rose 6.9% y/y in September, up from 3.6% in August. [InstaForex](https://www.instaforex.com/forex-news/3238651)
- I did not get an October figure from a past year in a usable form. One Trading Economics headline reads "Increases in October", apparently for 2025. [TE](https://tradingeconomics.com/new-zealand/credit-card-spending/news/501505)

## 5. Other forecasts
- No prediction market covers this NZ series. The Kalshi markets in the collected data cover US company card spend (Amazon, McDonald's and others) and do not match this question.
- Polymarket has NZ election markets (National at 0.70 to win, ending 2026-11-08). They are not directly relevant.
- I found no economist consensus for the October ECT figure. Trading Economics publishes a forecast, but I could not retrieve it.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Early November (likely around 4 to 6 Nov): Paymark/Worldline's October update and ANZ's October card spending report would be the best early indicators. Neither was published as of 2026-11-02.
- 2026-11-07/08: NZ general election. This is after October, so it does not affect the figure.
- 2026-11-12, 10:45am NZDT: Stats NZ "Electronic card transactions: October 2026". It may also revise September.
- After resolution: Selected price indexes (17 Nov), RBNZ credit card series (20 Nov).

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) About 10 days remain. Stats NZ publishes the October 2026 release on 12 November 2026 at 10:45am NZDT.

(b) The latest known value is September 2026: the seasonally adjusted total fell 0.5% (down $51 million), published 16 October 2026. August was about -0.9%, though I could not confirm that it is the total series rather than retail.

(c) If nothing changed, the month-on-month change would be about 0.0%. The no-change baseline for a growth rate is roughly flat, perhaps slightly negative if the recent weakness simply persists.

(d) If the current trend continued, I would expect a small decline of about -0.3 to -0.5%, based on two straight soft months, weak hospitality and apparel, and falling confidence. Against that:
- Petrol prices in October averaged clearly above September. They hit a record above $3.50 early in October, with 95-octane about 12% up on a month earlier. Fuel is roughly 5 to 6% of total card spending, so this mechanically adds about +0.2 to +0.4 percentage points to nominal spending.
- Some bounce back after two declines is also plausible.
- Netting these, my median is about +0.1%.

(e) Monthly moves in the total series are mostly within ±1%, with occasional swings of ±1.5 to 2.2% (for example, April at -1.6% and May at +2.2%). The standard deviation is roughly 1 percentage point, and signs alternate often.

(f) There is no matching market or published economist consensus. Paymark said September was a "slow start" to the pre-Christmas period, and Retail NZ describes retail as "under real pressure". Both lean slightly negative for real volumes, but nominal fuel spending provides support.

(g) Unexpected scenarios:
- Low outcome: an election-related pause in spending, wet weather, and a sharp drop in hospitality and durables, with the Labour Day and five-Saturday adjustment working against October. This could give -1.5 to -2%.
- High outcome: a fuel price spike combined with a rebound after two declines and an early start to Christmas or online sales, a May-style bounce. This could give +1.5 to +2%.

(c) **If nothing changed:** a flat month, roughly 0.0%.

(d) **If the current trend continued:** a mild decline of about -0.3 to -0.5%, since weak hospitality and discretionary spending would continue. Two other factors push the other way:
- Fuel prices were at record highs in early October. The 95-octane price was about 12.7% above a month earlier as of late October. Fuel is about 5 to 6% of total card spending, so a 4 to 6% rise in average fuel spending adds roughly +0.2 to +0.3 percentage points mechanically.
- After two consecutive declines, some bounce back is plausible.

(e) **Historical variation:** monthly changes in the total series have a standard deviation of about 1 percentage point. Most fall within ±1%, with occasional moves of -1.6 to +2.2%.

(f) **Expert and market expectations:** there is no market or consensus forecast for this question. Paymark described a "slower start" to the pre-Christmas period. Retail NZ says retail is under pressure, and consumer confidence is below 100.

(g) **Unexpected scenarios:**
- **Low:** fuel prices start falling, consumers pull back sharply amid liquidations and election uncertainty, and seasonal adjustment interacts with the five Saturdays and Labour Day. The result could be around -2%.
- **High:** a fuel-price surge combines with a rebound in hospitality and durables after the weak months, or seasonal adjustment over-corrects for the calendar effects. The result could be around +2%.
